The Merit Section (Kǒng Gōngcáo) Administrator for Merit Affairs

was responsible for evaluations, leaves and missions, sacrificial ceremonies, ritual music, schools, memorials and petitions, correspondence, auspicious banquets, portents and anomalies, medicine, divination, arrangements, and funerals.
The Granary Section (Cāng Cáo) Administrator for Granary Affairs
managed land taxes, government offices, kitchens, granaries and storehouses, and marketplaces.
The Household Section (Hù Cáo) Administrator for Household Affairs

oversaw household registration, accounting records, roads, travel permits, tax exemption certificates, miscellaneous corvée duties, tax arrears, social status (commoner and base classes), fodder and firewood, inns, marriages, land disputes, and honoring the filial and fraternal.
The Fields Section (Tián Cáo) Administrator for Fields Affairs
was in charge of garden estates, land allotments (kǒufēn), hereditary lands (yǒngyè), and official entitlement lands (yīntián).
The Military Section (Bīng Cáo) Administrator for Military Affairs
managed military officer selection, weapons and armor, equipment and insignia, gate controls and keys, garrison defense, beacon towers, courier stations, and hunting.
The Legal Section (Fǎ Cáo) Administrator for Legal Affairs
handled trials and application of laws, pursuit of robbers and bandits, and confiscation of illicit goods.
The Works Section (Shì Cáo) Administrator for Works Affairs
was responsible for bridges and ferries, boats and vehicles, buildings and residences, and crafts.
